# BLS Model exploration

read in data
```{r}
base <- read_csv("VBRescue_BLS_Shiny_download_only/bls_2026_updated.csv")

emts <- data.frame(date = base$date, bls_emts = base$bls_emts)
```

## linear regression
### single
```{r}
base_df <- base[,-2]

x<-as.numeric(difftime(base$date,base$date[1],units='days'))/30.4375
y<-base_df$bls_emts

slm <- lm(y~x)
summary(slm)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(slm)
```

### multiple
```{r}
plot(base_df$bls_emts,type='l', xlab='month', ylab="Number of BLS EMTs", main="Number of BLS EMTs" )
```
curved pattern shown. We will try the log transformation first, and also try a polynomial regression later. 

```{r}
base_df$log_y <- log(base_df$bls_emts)
plot(base_df$log_y,type='l', xlab='month', ylab="Log Number of BLS EMTs", main="Log Number of BLS EMTs" )
```
Not big improvement on curve pattern, but we will finish the linear model analysis with log transformation for now
```{r}
cor_matrix <- cor(base_df, use = "complete.obs")
cor_matrix 
```

Based on the correlation and using a threshold of 0.6 absolute value, month, emt_students, ops_pending, and bls_interns are the top predictors that are highly correlated to bls_emts. 

For Multicollinearity,
```{r}
cor_matrix1 <- cor(base_df, use = "complete.obs")
cor_matrix1 
corrplot(cor_matrix1, method = "color", col=COL2('RdBu'))
```

For multicollinearity issue: 
- month with pending_academy, and testing
- emt_students with pending_bls_interns, bls_interns, and ops_completions
- ops_pending with bls_interns, and emt_students
- bls_interns with emt_students, ops_pending, and ops_completion

With the limited data points, we will use high correlation predictors only 

```{r}
library(leaps)
lm_df <- base_df[,c(1, 5, 7, 17)]

# best R^2 adj.
coef(alllmreg, which.max(summary(alllmreg)$adjr2))
```
```{r}

```
```{r}
#best BIC
coef(alllmreg, which.min(summary(alllmreg)$bic))
```
For all bests: month, emt_students, ops_pending

```{r}

summary(emts_lm1)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

```

```{r}
summary(emts_lm1.1)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(emts_lm1.1)
```
bls_emts ~ month+emt_students+ops_pending seems to be the best combination of predictors if we want to do MLR (should we log the y for slightly better residual linearity?)


## Polynomial regression

Because we see a curved pattern, we want to try with the polynomial regression as well
We will still use the previous combination of variables we found using regsubsets()

```{r}
plot(base_df$month, base_df$bls_emts)
plot(base_df$emt_students, base_df$bls_emts)
plot(base_df$ops_pending, base_df$bls_emts)
```


Month show pretty moderate curved pattern, so we will start from there

```{r}
emts_poly1 <- lm(bls_emts ~ poly(month, 2)+ ops_pending + emt_students, data = base_df) 
summary(emts_poly1)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(emts_poly1)
```

The polynomial regression does not perform well and the 2nd degree month predictor is not significant, so we will rule out this. 


## Time Series
```{r}
plot(emts)

l_emts <- log(emts$bls_emts) #stabilize variance
emts_ts<-ts(l_emts,frequency=12,start=c(2026,1))
plot(emts_ts,type='l', xlab='month', ylab="Log Number of BLS EMTs", main="Log Number of BLS EMTs" )
points(emts_ts,pch=1,cex=0.6)

```
- We see a curved trend that generally positively growing. -> Gonna remove the positive trend using first difference so we isolate out seasonal trend

```{r}
emts_diff1 <- diff(emts_ts)

plot(emts_diff1,type='l', xlab='year', 
     ylab="diff", main="After diff1" ) #generally no trend now
points(emts_diff1,pch=1,cex=0.7)
lag.plot(emts_diff1, lags=6, do.lines=FALSE)
```
No clear seasonal trend shown as only lag 6 shows positive linear trend, while all other lag plots showing no clear positive trend. We will rule out any seasonal component for now since we don't have too much data point supporting it. 

The data is generally stationary, with slightly funnel out trend for the variance. 
```{r}
acf(emts_diff1, main="ACF of Log EMTs (diff 2)")
```
No significant lags shown in the acf plot, so we probably don't want to use time series. 

#ML setup

Split data
```{r}
set.seed(2026)

test_id  <- 9

n <- nrow(base[-9,])
id <- c(1:n)

train_id <- id[1:5]
valid_id <- id[6:8]


train <- base[train_id, ]
valid <- base[valid_id, ]
test  <- base[test_id, ]
dev <- rbind(train, valid) 

dim(train)
```
CV implementation
```{r}
set.seed(2026)
fold_id <- sample(rep(1:4, length.out = nrow(dev)))
degrees <- 1:4
table(fold_id)

cv_mse <- function(train_df, model_pred_func,
                   outcome = "bls_emts",
                   date_col = "date",
                   initial_window = 4,
                   horizon = 1,
                   step = 1) {

  # Sort observations chronologically
  train_df <- train_df[
    order(train_df[[date_col]]), 
  ]

  n <- nrow(train_df)

  if (initial_window < 2 || initial_window >= n) {
    stop("initial_window must be between 2 and nrow(train_df) - 1.")
  }

  if (horizon < 1 || step < 1 ||
      initial_window + horizon > n) {
    stop("Invalid horizon or step.")
  }

  squared_errors <- numeric(0)

  # Expanding-window CV
  for (origin in seq(
    from = initial_window,
    to = n - horizon,
    by = step
  )) {

    train_fold <- train_df[1:origin, , drop = FALSE]

    holdout_fold <- train_df[
      (origin + 1):(origin + horizon),
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    # Fit on the past and predict the future
    pred <- model_pred_func(train_fold, holdout_fold)

    if (length(pred) != nrow(holdout_fold)) {
      stop("Prediction count does not match holdout size.")
    }

    actual <- holdout_fold[[outcome]]

    squared_errors <- c(
      squared_errors,
      (actual - as.numeric(pred))^2
    )
  }

  mean(squared_errors, na.rm = TRUE)
}

```


## KNN
* I am going to do two combinations of predictors for KNN models. One would only take the month (act as generally ordering) and another takes the high correlation predictors we found in linear regression exploration

### Only Month
subset data and standardize month
```{r}
train_m <- train[,c(1,10)]
val_m <- validate[,c(1,10)]
test_m <- test[,c(1,10)]

train_center_m <- sapply(train_m[c("month")], mean)
train_scale_m  <- sapply(train_m[c("month")], sd)

standardize <- function(df, center, scale) {
  x <- as.matrix(df[c("month")])
  x <- sweep(x, 2, center, "-")
  sweep(x, 2, scale, "/")
}

x_train_m <- standardize(train_m, train_center_m, train_scale_m)
x_val_m <- standardize(val_m, train_center_m, train_scale_m)
x_test_m  <- standardize(test_m, train_center_m, train_scale_m)

```

```{r}
knn_reg_predict <- function(x_train, y_train, x_new, k) {
  sapply(seq_len(nrow(x_new)), function(i) {
    difference <- x_train - matrix(
      x_new[i, ], nrow = nrow(x_train), ncol = ncol(x_train),
      byrow = TRUE
    )
    distance_squared <- rowSums(difference^2)
    neighbor_id <- order(distance_squared)[seq_len(k)]
    mean(y_train[neighbor_id])
  })
}
```

```{r}
k_values <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)

results_m <- do.call(rbind, lapply(k_values, function(k) {
  pred_train <- knn_reg_predict(x_train_m, train_m$bls_emts, x_train_m, k)
  pred_validate  <- knn_reg_predict(x_train_m, train_m$bls_emts, x_val_m, k)

  data.frame(
    k = k,
    training_mse = mse(train_m$bls_emts, pred_train),
    validate_mse = mse(val_m$bls_emts, pred_validate)
  )
}))

results_m
```
```{r}
plot(results_m$k, results_m$training_mse,
     type = "o", pch = 19, col = "gray40",
     xlab = "K", ylab = "Mean squared error",
     ylim = range(results_m[c("training_mse", "validate_mse")]))
lines(results_m$k, results_m$validate_mse,
      type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#0072B2")
legend("topleft", c("Training MSE", "Validate MSE"),
       col = c("gray40", "#0072B2"), pch = 19, lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

Seems like K=5 is the best shot with our current data if only use month as predictor.

```{r}
month_knn_pred <- data.frame(
  original_y = val_m$bls_emts,
  predicted_y = knn_reg_predict(x_train_m, train_m$bls_emts, x_val_m, k=5)
)
month_knn_pred
```

### CV adaptation
```{r}
knn_wrapper <- function(train, new, predictor_cols, k) {

  # Extract predictors as matrices
  x_train <- as.matrix(train[, predictor_cols, drop = FALSE])
  x_new   <- as.matrix(new[, predictor_cols, drop = FALSE])

  y_train <- train$bls_emts

  # Standardize using training-fold statistics only
  x_mean <- colMeans(x_train)
  x_sd   <- apply(x_train, 2, sd)

  # Avoid division by zero for constant predictors
  x_sd[!is.finite(x_sd) | x_sd == 0] <- 1

  x_train_scaled <- scale(
    x_train,
    center = x_mean,
    scale = x_sd
  )

  x_new_scaled <- scale(
    x_new,
    center = x_mean,
    scale = x_sd
  )

  # K cannot exceed the training sample size
  k_use <- min(k, nrow(x_train_scaled))

  knn_reg_predict(
    x_train = x_train_scaled,
    y_train = y_train,
    x_new = x_new_scaled,
    k = k_use
  )
}
```

Month only model
```{r}
knn_time_model <- function(train, new, k = 3) {

  origin_date <- min(train$date)

  train$time_index <- as.numeric(
    difftime(train$date, origin_date, units = "days")
  ) / 30.4375

  new$time_index <- as.numeric(
    difftime(new$date, origin_date, units = "days")
  ) / 30.4375

  knn_wrapper(
    train = train,
    new = new,
    predictor_cols = "time_index",
    k = k
  )
}
```

lm_df approach KNN
```{r}
mlr_predictors <- c(
  "time_index",
  "emt_students",
  "ops_pending"
)

knn_mlr_model <- function(train, new, k = 3) {

  origin_date <- min(train$date)

  train$time_index <- as.numeric(
    difftime(train$date, origin_date, units = "days")
  ) / 30.4375

  new$time_index <- as.numeric(
    difftime(new$date, origin_date, units = "days")
  ) / 30.4375

  knn_wrapper(
    train = train,
    new = new,
    predictor_cols = mlr_predictors,
    k = k
  )
}
```

```{r}
pred_train_lm <- lm(formula = bls_emts ~ month+emt_students+ops_pending, data = train_lm)
pred_val_lm  <- predict.lm(pred_train_lm, newdata=val_lm[,-4])
MLR_best <-data.frame(

MLR_best
```

```{r}
mlr_model <- function(train, new) {

  origin_date <- min(train$date)

  train$time_index <- as.numeric(
    difftime(train$date, origin_date, units = "days")
  ) / 30.4375

  new$time_index <- as.numeric(
    difftime(new$date, origin_date, units = "days")
  ) / 30.4375

  fit <- lm(bls_emts ~ time_index+emt_students+ops_pending, data = train)

  predict(fit, newdata = new)
}
```

### Compare with Endpoint (already implemented)

```{r}
endpoint_pred <- function(train_df, new_df){
  x_train <- as.numeric(
    difftime(train_df$date, train_df$date[1], units = "days")
  ) / 30.4375

  y_train <- train_df$bls_emts
  
  slope <- (tail(y_train, 1) - head(y_train, 1)) /
    (tail(x_train, 1) - head(x_train, 1))

  if (!is.finite(slope)) {
    stop("Cannot estimate trend from training dates")
  }

  last_date <- tail(train_df$date, 1)
  current <- tail(y_train, 1)

  elapsed <- as.numeric(
    difftime(new_df$date, last_date, units = "days")
  ) / 30.4375

  pred <- pmax(0, current + slope * elapsed)

  return(pred)
}

train_ep <- train[,c(2,10)]
val_ep <- validate[,c(2,10)]
test_ep <- test[,c(2,10)]

pred_train_end <- endpoint_pred(train_ep, train_ep[,-2])
pred_val_end  <- endpoint_pred(train_ep, val_ep[,-2])
ep_perf <-data.frame(
  method = "Endpoint",
  training_mse = mse(train_lm$bls_emts, pred_train_end),
  validate_mse = mse(val_lm$bls_emts, pred_val_end)
) 
```


# Comparison table

```{r}
models <- list(
  Endpoint = endpoint_pred,
  SLR = lm_time_model,
  MLR = mlr_model
)

k_values <- c(2, 3, 4, 5)

# Add KNN models for each k
for (k in k_values) {

  models[[paste0("KNN_Time_k", k)]] <-
    local({
      kk <- k
      function(train, new) {
        knn_time_model(train, new, k = kk)
      }
    })

  models[[paste0("KNN_MLR_k", k)]] <-
    local({
      kk <- k
      function(train, new) {
        knn_mlr_model(train, new, k = kk)
      }
    })
}

cv_results <- data.frame(
  Model = names(models),
  CV_MSE = sapply(models, function(model_func) {
    cv_mse(
      train_df = dev,
      model_pred_func = model_func,
      outcome = "bls_emts",
      date_col = "date",
      initial_window = 4,
      horizon = 1
    )
  })
)

cv_results <- cv_results[order(cv_results$CV_MSE), ]
rownames(cv_results) <- NULL

print(cv_results)
```

```{r}
  cv_results[order(cv_results$CV_MSE), ],
  5
)

print(top5)

```

```{r}
top5_names <- top5$Model

test_results <- data.frame(
  Model = top5_names,
  CV_MSE = top5$CV_MSE,
  Test_MSE = sapply(top5_names, function(model_name) {

    pred <- models[[model_name]](dev, test)

    mean(
      (test$bls_emts - as.numeric(pred))^2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  })
)

test_results <- test_results[order(test_results$CV_MSE), ]
rownames(test_results) <- NULL

print(test_results)
```
